name: Vox Royalty Corp.
business_overview: Vox Royalty Corp. operates as a mining royalty company. The company holds a portfolio of 70 precious metals royalties in Australia, Canada, the United States of America, South Africa, Brazil, and Peru. The company was founded in 2014 and is based in Westminster, Colorado.

classification_meta.logic_summary: Mining royalty company holding a diversified portfolio of precious metals royalties, generating licensing revenue from mining operators.

narrative.text:
**Business & market dynamics:** Vox’s core royalty operations are benefiting from strong momentum and extended mine lives, such as the Bonikro gold mine now projected through 2036, which improves cash flow visibility. The portfolio is gold-focused, where producer activity reinforces revenue durability. The shares trade at a marked discount to peers on a per-royalty-ounce basis, hinting at underappreciated asset quality.

**Management strategy and execution:** Management raised full-year guidance, initiated a quarterly dividend, and set a 2030 royalty receipt target, demonstrating confidence and a shareholder-return mindset. The company is debt-free with an undrawn credit line, preserving strategic flexibility. Growing institutional ownership and a new Buy-rated analyst initiation add external validation to management’s plan.

Shares of Vox Royalty Corp., whose business is built on royalties from gold miners, jumped 4.3% in extended trading on Wednesday to $6.55 apiece before giving up almost all of those gains. The company reported what it called “exceptional results” for the first quarter and raised its guidance for the full-year 2026.

## Details

Vox shares rose as much as 4.3% in extended trading on Wednesday to $6.55 apiece. But by premarket trading on Thursday, the stock was up just 0.2%.
